units.spine: The town knows precisely what it could not survive, and shapes what it dares and does not dare around that knowledge.
What Warmholz's defenses are ordinarily worth does not describe the town at present. A crisis is on it, and the defenses have been rebuilt around that crisis.
A crisis has changed how Warmholz defends itself and not whether it can support itself, and the two have been kept apart.

units.poolKey: COMPOUND override (a crisis stress has rewritten the label)
units.spine: The ordinary safety of Warmholz has stopped applying. Whatever the town was before, a monster threat is what governs its streets now.

units.poolKey: First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)
units.spine: Only a first look has been taken of Warmholz's safety. It says plainly what has been seen and nothing about what has not.
No organized crime has been identified at Warmholz. Whatever wrongdoing the town has does not run through anything that could be called an organization.
The Free Elder Council at Warmholz has had nothing criminal reach it. Whatever operates in the town runs outside the council, and its decisions remain its own.
A stranger walks into Warmholz from whatever side he chooses, and is not made to pass anybody on the way in.
A stranger at Warmholz can find nobody whose task the town's defense is, because it is nobody's task at all.

units.poolKey: charter hall ABSENT where the country warrants one
units.spine: Warmholz has no charter hall to answer for its defense, so soldiers wrong for the work are sent instead, and the town pays for that wrongness every time.
Nothing unseen has come at Warmholz, and nothing here would know if it had. What counts as safe and what could be caught are two different things.
Too small to need a wall, and the town knows it well enough. Its safety is its neighbours, its distance, and its own unimportance.
The town holds no food store of its own. Any break in its road access cuts off supply within days, not seasons.
